input.reason: The request is a display-ordering concern of the watchlist view, so the watchlist component's movies signal should become a stable unwatched-first partition of the store's items. The store (and every other unit) stays untouched, so persistence and all other consumers are unaffected.

steps.instruction: Reorder the watchlist so unwatched movies are shown before watched ones. The `movies` signal must derive from the store's items as a stable partition: every item with watched === false first, then every item with watched === true, preserving the store's order within each group (equivalently: a stable sort of store.items() by the watched flag). `movies()` must still return exactly the same items the store holds - same set, nothing added, dropped or duplicated - and it must remain fully reactive: when an item's watched status is toggled (via the store or the component's toggleWatched), movies() must immediately reflect the new grouping. Make sure the template renders the rows from movies() (if it currently iterates store.items() directly, switch it to movies()) so the visible list follows this order. Keep all other behaviour (remove, toggle, watchedCount, progress, announcements) and all public signatures unchanged. Do not change watchlist-store: its items order and persistence stay exactly as they are.

testChangeReasons.reason: This test re-queried the first row's checkbox after clicking it. Under the new required ordering (unwatched movies first), the movie just toggled to watched is re-ordered to the end of the list, so the first checkbox after the click belongs to the other, still-unwatched movie and `checkbox().checked` would be false, failing the test even though the component behaves correctly. I captured a reference to the clicked checkbox before the click and assert on that element; the test's original intent (clicking a checkbox marks that movie watched) and the watchedCount/subtitle assertions are unchanged.
testChangeReasons.title: Watchlist > toggles watched when the checkbox is clicked

testChangeReasons.reason: Same consequence of the new ordering: after clicking blank space on the first row, that movie becomes watched and its row is re-ordered to the end, so re-querying the first row's checkbox no longer finds the toggled movie's checkbox and the test would fail despite correct behaviour. The test now holds a reference to the clicked row's checkbox before clicking, preserving its original intent (a blank-space row click toggles that row's movie).

 })
 export class Watchlist {
